alice_infra: Heads up — after the kernel/driver push at 03:00 UTC, a subset of H100 nodes in us-west2 are flapping and failing inference workloads. Seeing a lot of JIT/PTX compile errors and occasional PCIe link resets. :warning:

alice_infra: Root cause still unknown, but symptoms: model pods OOMing on compile, then node-level NV driver kernel logs show symbol lookup failures. Sample from /var/log/kern.log:
```
[Mar 18 03:12:45 node-h100-17 kernel] nvidia: failed to load PTX module: signature mismatch for sm_90 kernel 
[Mar 18 03:12:46 node-h100-17 kernel] NVRM: GPU at 0000:3d:00.0: pci read error, disabling device
[Mar 18 03:12:46 node-h100-17 kernel] pci 0000:3d:00.0: AER: reported fatal error: PCIe replay timeout
```

ben_driver: Hmm, signature mismatch + PCIe errs -> smells like mismatched driver/CUDA/toolkit artifacts vs compiled kernels. Did the upgrade force a minimum driver ABI we don't match? Which driver version is live?

alice_infra: The rollout put nvidia-driver 535.113 -> 536.45 clusterwide. CUDA runtime packages on some images still point to 12.1 / compiled cubin blob set for previous toolchain. Canary hosts reported at 03:05, then we started seeing failovers.

charlie_oncall: Observed NCCL hangs in allreduce on multi-node jobs shortly before GPU flaps. Logs show: "nccl: CUDA fatal error: either unrecognized PTX or failed JIT" then gpu resets. Jobs get rescheduled and run into the same node again because autoscaler pins preferred zones.

dana_mlinfra: Quick mitigation options: 1) force runtime to use precompiled CUBIN (skip PTX JIT) for sm_90 where available; 2) set env to disable ptx JIT fallback (I can push a kube patch); 3) roll back driver to 535.* on H100 pool only. Which is least risky?

ben_driver: Rolling back is safest short-term but impacts the driver rollout we already planned (security+stability fixes). We can try (1) first: set REDWOOD_INFER_DISABLE_PTX_JIT=1 in node daemonset or pod runtime so loader prefers cubin. Runtime has a flag: --prefers-cubin or env NVIDIA_DISABLE_PTX_JIT=1 on our fork. That should avoid JIT compile mismatch.

norris_sre: I'll patch a kube node-label selector to target only h100-pool and apply a DaemonSet change with env var. I want to do it on canary nodes (2 nodes) first and see if pods stabilize before a full-scale patch. Also we should update scheduler so it doesn't co-locate big NCCL jobs on potentially flaky hosts.

deploy-bot: deploy request: ds/h100-runtime-patch -> rollout started on k8s/us-west2-canary (2/2 updated). Checks: liveness OK, pods in crashloop: 0.

charlie_oncall: Canary looks promising: JIT errors gone on the two patched hosts. No PCIe replay messages in last 15m. NCCL jobs that were failing are now proceeding (slow start but stable).

alice_infra: Good. Let's keep canary for 1 hour then promote. Meanwhile, SRE to prepare a driver-rollback playbook just in case. We need to log cost impact: autoscaler churn + job retries added ~4k USD in token-hour equivalent this morning. Add to incident runbook.

ben_driver: Action items: (A) Update runtime code to detect PTX signature mismatch and auto-fallback to cubin (ticket INF-8421), (B) add a preflight that verifies driver ABI vs compiled model artifacts during image bake, (C) coordinate with infra ops to re-run driver rollout with H100-specific gating.

norris_sre: Creating rollback runbook now. It includes steps to cordon H100 nodes, drain non-critical workloads, apply apt-get install nvidia-driver-535.xx, restart nvidia pods, and monitor kernel/AER logs. Will also include commands to blacklist ptx_jit plugin if needed.

dana_mlinfra: Also adding a prompt to the model onboarding checklist: 'include sm_90 cubin artifact or mark image as ptx-jit-required' — avoids runtime surprises. I'll open a PR in infra-images.

alice_infra: Summary for postmortem: kernel/driver upgrade exposed PTX/CUBIN ABI mismatch for SM90 (Hopper) on a subset of images. Mitigated by forcing precompiled cubin usage on runtime; plan to harden bake-time checks and implement auto-fallback. Keep monitoring us-west2; if we see any PCIe AERs reappear we rollback driver on H100 pool.

charlie_oncall: I'll leave the incident channel open and run 30m extra checks on NCCL perf. If anything pops up I will @here. :white_check_mark:
